instrucciones: 5. Choose ONLY 3 of the following situations and WRITE what you would say in each one to show that you understand the context of the situation. Write between 10 and 25 words. (1.5 points) Only the first three you answer will be marked.

items.enunciado: a) Your friend says, “Summer camps abroad are a waste of money because you can learn English at home.” Give your opinion.
items.modelo: I don’t think so. At a camp you speak English all day with people from other countries, and that is much harder to do at home.

items.enunciado: b) Your cousin is nervous about going to a camp in Ireland for the first time. Advise him.

titulo: Training after class: how students balance sport and study
instrucciones: Read the text and answer questions 1, 2 and 3. In question 1, copy the exact words from the text as evidence; in question 2, copy no more than 10 words; in question 3, find the word in the text that matches each definition.
texto:
At seventeen, Lucía Marín gets up at six every morning. She has swimming practice before school, lessons until three, and then two more hours of training in the evening. Her homework is usually done on the bus or after dinner. Lucía is one of a growing number of young people in Spain who combine serious sport with their studies, and she admits that it is not always easy.

Schools and sports clubs are starting to help students like her. In some towns, young athletes can attend a special timetable that allows them to leave class early for training. Teachers also send notes and exercises by email when a student has to travel to a competition. “Without this support, I would have given up my studies or my sport,” Lucía says. “Now I can keep doing both.”

Experts say that the benefits are clear. According to Dr Hugo Salas, a sports psychologist, students who train regularly are usually better at organising their time. “They learn that every hour counts, so they waste less of it,” he explains. Sport also teaches them to deal with pressure and to accept failure, two skills that are very useful during exams.

However, the risks should not be ignored. Many young athletes sleep fewer than seven hours a night, and some suffer from constant tiredness or injuries. Dr Salas warns that parents and teachers must watch for signs of stress. “A talented teenager is still a teenager,” he says. “Rest and friends are as important as medals.”

For the moment, only a small number of schools offer flexible timetables, and most families have to pay for private classes to help their children catch up. Lucía hopes this will change soon. She wants to study physiotherapy at university, and she is determined to continue swimming at the same time. “It is hard work,” she says, “but I would not change it for anything.”

items.pregunta: 1. Say whether the following sentences are TRUE or FALSE according to the text. COPY the evidence from the text. No marks will be given without the evidence. (1.5 points)
items.afirmacion: a) Lucía does all her homework at school before training.
pruebas: Her homework is usually done on the bus or after dinner
homework is usually done on the bus or after dinner
items.explicacion: FALSE: Lucía hace los deberes en el autobús o después de cenar, no en el colegio. La prueba hay que copiarla tal cual del texto, sin puntos suspensivos ni número de línea.

items.afirmacion: b) Teachers sometimes help athletes who are away at competitions.
pruebas: Teachers also send notes and exercises by email when a student has to travel to a competition
send notes and exercises by email when a student has to travel to a competition
items.explicacion: TRUE: los profesores envían apuntes y ejercicios por correo cuando el alumno viaja a una competición.

items.afirmacion: c) Most schools in Spain already offer flexible timetables for athletes.
pruebas: only a small number of schools offer flexible timetables
For the moment, only a small number of schools offer flexible timetables
items.explicacion: FALSE: solo unos pocos colegios ofrecen horarios flexibles, no la mayoría.

instrucciones: 6. Choose ONE of the following topics and WRITE a composition of about 140-180 words. If you choose the email, DO NOT SIGN it. (3 points)

items.enunciado: a) Should students have a part-time job or play a sport while they study? Give your opinion.
items.modelo:
Nowadays many students are very busy with homework and exams, so it is worth asking whether they should also do a part-time activity such as sport. In my opinion, playing a sport is a great idea, as long as it does not take too much time.

First of all, sport is good for our health. After sitting in class for hours, we need to move and breathe fresh air. Moreover, training with a team teaches us to cooperate and to accept defeat, which are useful skills for life.

Secondly, exercise helps us study better. When I go for a run in the afternoon, I feel less stressed and I can concentrate more easily. Besides, a timetable with sport forces us to organise our time well.

However, some students have too many activities and get tired, so their marks go down. For this reason, it is important to choose only one or two days a week.

In conclusion, I think combining study and sport is positive for young people because it keeps body and mind healthy, but we must find a balance.
criterios: Presentación: párrafos claros, puntuación correcta.
Organización: estructura del tipo de texto (email; for & against; opinion essay), registro adecuado, ideas enlazadas con conectores.
Contenido: me ciño al tema, ideas suficientes y variadas, sin repeticiones.
Corrección gramatical: frases bien construidas, variedad de estructuras, sin traducir del español.
Vocabulario: rico y no copiado del texto; menos de 4 faltas de ortografía (más de 3 restan).
items.explicacion: Opinion essay: introducción con la postura, un párrafo por idea con conectores (first of all, moreover, besides, however, in conclusion), conclusión. Entre 140 y 180 palabras: por debajo de 140 baja el tope de nota.

items.enunciado: b) Write an email to a friend telling him or her about the new sports club you have joined after school and inviting your friend to try a free class with you.
items.modelo:
Hi Daniel,

How are things? I hope you are enjoying the new school year. I’m writing to tell you about something I started a few weeks ago and that I’m really excited about.

I have joined a basketball club that meets twice a week after school. At first I was a bit nervous because I had never played in a team, but the coach is very patient and the other players are really friendly. We practise for an hour and then we usually have a snack together. The best thing is that I feel more energetic and I sleep much better than before.

The club offers a free class for newcomers every Thursday. Why don’t you come with me next week? You don’t need any special clothes, only trainers and a bottle of water. Afterwards we could go for an ice cream and chat about everything.

Tell me if you can come. I’m sure you’ll have a great time!

See you soon,
criterios: Presentación: párrafos claros, puntuación correcta.
Organización: estructura del tipo de texto (email; for & against; opinion essay), registro adecuado, ideas enlazadas con conectores.
Contenido: me ciño al tema, ideas suficientes y variadas, sin repeticiones.
Corrección gramatical: frases bien construidas, variedad de estructuras, sin traducir del español.
Vocabulario: rico y no copiado del texto; menos de 4 faltas de ortografía (más de 3 restan).
items.explicacion: Email informal: saludo, motivo, cuerpo contando el club con tus palabras (qué haces, cómo te sientes), invitación («Why don’t you come…?») y despedida SIN firmar.
